Every transitivity triple containing a new variable has at most two parameters, since the fixed complete height-two parameter order has no strict parameter chain of length two, making 3-/4-point state compatibility necessary and sufficient. The six/seven states and compatible support matrices are explicitly enumerated; substitution X=exp(s)-1, Y=exp(t)-1 and exact coefficient extraction prove the stated formulas for all a,b>=0. An independent direct relation-assignment enumerator checks all a+b<=4, with exact checks for 192 additional symbolic coefficient cases. Balanced asymptotics follow from dominant bases. Risks: implementation or transcription error beyond these exact checks; no unproved enumeration is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The two-orientation exact spectrum measures stabilizer-orbit complexity in the canonical countable universal homogeneous poset and handles a naturally motivated infinite family of genuinely comparable two-level parameter sets. Unlike the one-level antichain restriction, the formula shows that balanced growth makes pair comparability exponentially rare, with sharp factor 2*(9/16)^n. The explicit closed form and orientation split have exact mathematical meaning for all a,b and can be used to study conditioned finite-type distributions, rather than merely providing a tiny arbitrary census. The proof does not extend to arbitrary height-two bases or arity >=3.
